extra.message: Server-side JavaScript injection / Remote Code Execution: handleContributionsUpdate passes raw, unvalidated POST body values (req.body.preTax, req.body.afterTax, req.body.roth) directly to eval() (lines 32-34). An attacker can submit arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('cmd')) which executes with the full privileges of the Node.js process. The comments on lines 37-41 document that parseInt() was the intended safe alternative.

NoSQL / JavaScript injection into MongoDB: the user-controlled 'threshold' value (from req.query.threshold, see app/routes/allocations.js:19-23) is concatenated unvalidated into a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression: `this.userId == ... && this.stocks > '${threshold}'`. An attacker can inject arbitrary JS that MongoDB executes, e.g. `1'; while(true){} '` for a denial of service, or `1'; return 1=='1 '` to bypass filtering and read other users' allocation data. Only parseInt() of userId is done; threshold is never sanitized (the intended fix is documented in the commented lines 64-76).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery: displayResearch builds a URL from the fully attacker-controlled query parameters req.query.url + req.query.symbol and fetches it with needle.get(), then streams the response body back to the client. Although the research.html form provides a default 'url' hidden field, an attacker can set ?url=http://169.254.169.254/... (cloud metadata) or any internal-only host and the server will fetch it and disclose the response, allowing internal network scanning and access to internal services.

Broken function-level access control / missing authorization: GET and POST /benefits are protected only by isLoggedIn and never by isAdminUserMiddleware (defined at app/routes/session.js:25 but unused), even though the intended fix is documented in the comment on lines 57-60. Any authenticated non-admin user can therefore view the full list of non-admin users (PII in app/routes/benefits.js:15-20) and POST an arbitrary userId + benefitStartDate to modify other users' benefit records (benefits-dao.updateBenefits, app/data/benefits-dao.js:23-40). Privilege escalation to admin functions.

Insecure Direct Object Reference: displayAllocations takes userId from req.params.userId (destructured on lines 16-18) instead of from req.session.userId (the fix is documented in the commented lines 12-15). Since /allocations/:userId is mounted with only isLoggedIn middleware, any authenticated user can change the URL parameter to view another user's allocation data (DAO lookup by arbitrary userId in app/data/allocations-dao.js:57-110).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Stored cross-site scripting: the global nav renders the DB-stored user fields {{firstName}} {{lastName}} with no escaping, and swig autoescaping is globally disabled in server.js:137 (autoescape: false). firstName/lastName are attacker-controlled: the signup validator only constrains length (/^.{1,100}$/, app/routes/session.js:163-170) and /profile allows updating them freely. A payload such as <script>...</script> stored in a user profile executes in the browser of every logged-in user who views any page (including admins on /benefits via benefits.html:51-52), enabling session hijacking.

extra.message: Reflected cross-site scripting: on a failed login the raw userName POST field is echoed back into value="{{userName}}" (set in app/routes/session.js:83 and rendered here) with no sanitization and global swig autoescaping disabled (server.js:137). An attacker can craft a login URL/username like "><script>alert(document.cookie)</script> that reflects and executes in the victim's browser when the (nonexistent) account fails to authenticate.

extra.message: Reflected (and stored) cross-site scripting: on a failed bankRouting validation, handleProfileUpdate re-renders the profile page with firstNameSafeString = raw, unencoded firstName (app/routes/profile.js:64-75) and this template interpolates it both in value="{{firstNameSafeString}}" (line 41) and inside an href attribute (line 78) with autoescaping disabled. Note the developer only encodes doc.website for HTML (profile.js:28) — firstName/lastName from the DB are otherwise rendered raw across every page (see layout.html:75), so stored firstName values also trigger XSS.

extra.message: Open redirect: GET /learn (protected only by isLoggedIn) redirects the browser directly to the user-controlled req.query.url value via res.redirect(req.query.url). An attacker can send a victim /learn?url=https://evil.example (or //evil.example) to phish credentials on an attacker-controlled look-alike site. The in-page fix comment (index.js:71) confirms this is intentionally insecure.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Regular expression denial of service (ReDoS): the regex /([0-9]+)+\#/ used to validate the user-supplied bankRouting field contains a nested quantifier (([0-9]+)+) whose greedy repetition of a greedy group causes catastrophic backtracking on long strings of digits without a trailing '#' (e.g. a few dozen digits), pinning the Node.js event loop and denying service. The vulnerable pattern is confirmed by the developer's own comment on lines 52-58 describing the fix.

Missing CSRF protection: the csurf import (line 7) and the csrf() middleware that would expose a token to templates are commented out (lines 104-113), and no token is validated on the state-changing POST endpoints (/profile, /contributions, /benefits, /memos — routes registered in app/routes/index.js). A logged-in victim can be forced by a malicious page to submit forged cross-origin POSTs (e.g. changing benefit dates, contribution percentages, or their own profile/bank data) because these handlers rely only on the session cookie.

Plaintext storage and comparison of passwords: addUser stores the raw password in the user document (line 25) because the bcrypt.hashSync(...) fix is commented out (lines 27-30), and validateLogin compares plaintext via fromDB === fromUser (line 61) with the bcrypt.compareSync fix commented out (lines 63-66). A database leak exposes every credential in cleartext; combined with the weak password policy /^.{1,20}$/ (app/routes/session.js:144) this allows trivial account compromise.

Hardcoded session signing secret and crypto key shipped in the default (and production) config: cookieSecret is the fixed value "session_cookie_secret_key_here" (line 8) and cryptoKey "a_secure_key_for_crypto_here" (line 9). Because express-session signs the session cookie with this secret (server.js:82), any attacker who knows it (it is in public source code) can forge a session cookie for an arbitrary userId — including an admin — without credentials, bypassing authentication entirely.

Sensitive information disclosure via the error handler: the catch-all error middleware logs err.stack to the console (error.js:7-8) and passes the entire err object into the view, which prints it with {{error}} in error-template.html:11 while swig autoescaping is disabled (server.js:137). Internal exception messages and stack traces (file paths, library internals, and any user data embedded in thrown errors) are disclosed to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Security misconfiguration of the session cookie: the express-session middleware uses the default cookie name (connect.sid) and the httpOnly/secure cookie options are commented out (lines 92-100), so the session identifier is readable by JavaScript and transmitted over the plaintext HTTP channel (http.createServer, line 145). Any XSS or network observer can steal a live session; saveUninitialized:true and resave:true also create unnecessary session state (CWE-614/CWE-1004).

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Session fixation: handleLoginRequest assigns req.session.userId directly (line 116) without regenerating the session ID on authentication; the required req.session.regenerate() wrapper is documented but commented out (lines 104-115). An attacker who fixes a victim's session ID before login can reuse that ID after the victim authenticates to impersonate them.

Log injection / log forging: the attacker-controlled userName submitted to the login form is written to the server log with console.log without sanitization (line 64). A userName containing CR/LF characters can forge arbitrary log lines and mislead log-based monitoring/forensics. The surrounding comments (lines 66-80) document the intended encoding fix that is not applied.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: Security misconfiguration: the application runs over cleartext HTTP (http.createServer, line 145) because the HTTPS setup is commented out (lines 149-155), and hardening is disabled — app.disable('x-powered-by') (leaks the Express version), helmet (frameguard/nocache/CSP/HSTS), and the nosniff middleware are all commented out (lines 38-65, 14). This exposes the app to traffic sniffing, clickjacking, MIME-sniffing and other header-based attacks.
